mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-32.9 to -30.7). This autocorrelated momentum in consumer foot traffic tends to persist in the near term, driving continued upward movement in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -32.9 to -30.7 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite three consecutive weeks of prior increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in PARKS mobility (9.3 to 26.7) signals increased willingness to leave home for leisure, which spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits once PARKS sustains an elevated level, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 25 points from baseline and stays there for at least one additional week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 26.7 at t-0w, nearly triple its t-3w value
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next two weeks even though PARKS remains above 25 for the following week.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility stabilizes (flat near -31 to -33) while TRANSIT mobility simultaneously improves (-44.4 to -41.3), the combination indicates resumed commuting patterns that generate incidental retail stops, jointly pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks more than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved by 3.1 points while WORKPLACES stayed within a 1-point band
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stays flat over the next four weeks despite TRANSIT improving further and WORKPLACES remaining stable.

mechanism_narrative: The strong and accelerating rise in PARKS mobility reflects a seasonal shift toward outdoor activity (e.g., warmer weather), which is historically associated with increased discretionary retail and recreation visits in the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS nearly tripled from 9.3 to 26.7 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the prior 28-day mean despite PARKS continuing to climb or hold above 25.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility crossing above a -40 threshold would indicate meaningful relaxation of transit-related restrictions or fear, which historically precedes a rebound in retail visits within two weeks as people resume broader movement.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -40 points from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -44.4 to -41.3, approaching the -40 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks after TRANSIT crosses above -40, or TRANSIT crosses but RETAIL_REC falls.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (around 9-10 throughout the snapshot) indicates a stable share of time spent at home, which creates a structural ceiling that limits how much RETAIL_REC can grow regardless of other improving indicators.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed within a narrow 9.0-10.1 band across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises substantially (more than 2 points average) over the next week while RESIDENTIAL remains flat or rises, contradicting the ceiling effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM improving in tandem with RETAIL_REC (both show consistent weekly gains) signals a broad-based recovery in essential-plus-discretionary consumer mobility; when both rise together in the same week, RETAIL_REC tends to continue rising the following week due to shared underlying consumer confidence.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -4.4 to -2.4 while RETAIL_REC rose from -32.9 to -30.7 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls over the next week despite GROCERY_PHARM also rising in the same prior week, breaking the co-movement pattern.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has slightly declined (-31.6 to -32.6) even as TRANSIT improves, suggesting a partial-reopening regime where remote work persists alongside loosening transit restrictions; this mixed signal caps retail recovery because weekday commuter-driven retail spending remains suppressed.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines or stays flat while TRANSIT improves by more than 2 points over two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell slightly from -31.6 to -32.6 while TRANSIT improved from -44.4 to -41.3
regime_hint: partial reopening with persistent remote work
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining flat or declining and TRANSIT continuing to improve.
